population: Six previously unmeasured full-length contest inputs. Generate two distributions for each of the existing Wall, Scrivener and Money for Nothing static programs. The two known controls are Wall/crossed_intervals and Scrivener/prefix_forks. Score all six prospective inputs even when a guest measures a shorter duration than anticipated. Compare each arm only against the native references for that exact input on that guest.
baseline: Use the first direct native observation after the input's complete footprint profile. Bind each normal work-clock policy to that input, executable, capture, CPU and boot. Collect all initial profiles and observations before starting the candidate rounds.
candidate: Visit every input once per round for three additional native rounds. Use the case ID SHA-256 order and rotate the start by 0, 1 and 2 respectively. Select the normal policy for the median of the three exact-input CPU times, breaking ties chronologically. Run both clocks live on each registered deadline with the usual independent 120-second watchdog.
limits: Each prospective input has fixed limits of 50, 100, 200 and 400 whole ms. The two known controls have 12, 13 and 14 ms. Add the ceiling of 85%, 100% and 115% of the first native estimate as whole ms on every input. Deduplicate the union, alternate arm order by registered case index plus limit index and enforce each arm once on each limit. Exceeding the limit is strict.
reference: Collect eleven subsequent native wait4 samples in rotating digest order after all paired enforcements on each guest. Trace workload PIDs on CPU 1, verify all outputs and counters, and replay both sets of actual decisions through the Aonohako reference. Use two independent AMD Milan GCE boots with one thread per core and identical collection payloads.
evaluation: Primary endpoint is median absolute relative duration error across the six new inputs versus each guest's independent per-input native medians. Require a reduction on both boots to call the duration gain replicated. Report maximum, signed error, wins/ties/losses, fixed and union verdict agreement with unanimous and majority native votes, and additional calibration CPU. Report earlier controls separately. Compare fixed limits across guests and give native durations so the coverage of longer runs is explicit.
boundary_diagnostic: Before looking at references, flag each distinct input/deadline when the three candidate calibration samples give both a pass and a timeout: min(samples) <= limit < max(samples). Separately count mixed native limits flagged and missed, flags on unanimous references, and actual candidate majority disagreements inside/outside the flagged group. This flag is descriptive; it never changes a deadline or verdict. Show prospective and control results separately, keeping boot and fixed/union counts distinct.
